summary: A dictionary matches keys to values, like names to scores. Use it when you look things up by a name instead of by a position.
notes: scores["Ben"] = 82 replaces the old value because keys are unique.
91 in scores is False because in only checks keys.
counts.get(food, 0) + 1 is the standard way to count items.
pitfall: scores["Zoe"] on a missing key stops the program with KeyError: 'Zoe'. Use get() or check with in first.
